newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude keeps slim gains late on spread buying.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude keeps slim gains late on spread buying.

text.p: NYMEX crude retained slim gains into Friday afternoon despite failing at key technical resistance as strength in IPE Brent spurred calendar spread buying.

"I think you have some good June/July spread buying (in favor of June) and the key reason is that Brent moved to a backwardation from contango and that took a lot people by surprise," said a New York crude trader.
At 1420 EDT, June crude was up nine cents a barrel at $20.42 after rising as high as $20.55, technical resistance and the spot month's highest level since April 1.

After solid gains early session, refined products were also slightly positive but in a holding pattern. Dealers said they were cautious about taking positions until crude provides a more definitive market direction.
"It seems like prices have been sitting here for two hours because its seems dangerous to do anything else," said a New York gasoline trader.
June gasoline was up 0.30 cent at 62.80 cents while June heating oil was up 0.27 cent at 54.65 cents a gallon.
"There was a healthy increase in open interest in crude yesterday with a lot of fund buying, so it seems that longs just don't want to leave," said a New York refined products dealer.

The NYMEX June/July crude spread had widened to a seven cent backwardation after settling at unchanged Thursday. June Brent on London's IPE set an eight cent backwardation to July from a 12 cent contango Wednesday.
Backwardation means the contract nearer in time is more expensive than the contract later in time. When a calendar spread is in contango the nearer contract is less expensive than the later contract.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
